cells.tense: You are here with the ending, clearing what has finished and keeping what still holds.
cells.ask: Tell one person this week what you have decided is over, then stop there and let the conversation close.
cells.core:
You are in the middle of a real ending and you are doing it with your eyes open. Something has been cleared, or you know exactly what is about to be, and you are not pretending otherwise. People can feel that in how you talk — what you stay with, what you leave alone, what you stop explaining.

That same pull toward connection runs while the old shape comes apart, not after it. You keep moving toward what matters while the rest finishes, which is the part most people skip. What you are carrying is the ending and the moving toward both, and holding them together costs something to keep. Notice what you are feeding next, because it is already close.
cells.sheetLine: You are ending this with your eyes open, and still reaching.
cells.verb: pulling what connects toward the end of what was
cells.place: the room where something has to finish before anything else can start

cells.tense: You are standing ahead of an ending that has not happened, trying to close a door early.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you keep rehearsing and do it badly today, before the timing feels right.
cells.core:
You are trying to force an ending that is not ready to close. A conversation in front of you turns into a chance to finish it, a silence turns into proof that it should already be over, and you are spending today on the shape of a day that is not here.

What you want underneath is something real and shared to hold onto. But you are pushing at it instead of letting it arrive, and that pushing takes away the thing you were pushing for. The clearing happens on its own schedule. You can make the move. You cannot make the timing. That difference is the whole of it.

cells.tense: You stopped moving toward people a while back, and you are at a door already behind you.
cells.ask: Write down what the situation actually needs, one page, and follow only the clearest line on it this week.
cells.core:
Something ended and you have not moved. Not out of grief exactly — you stopped moving toward people, and the ending in front of you closed a while back. You can describe it clearly. You just stopped doing anything about it.

The way back is not through more feeling. It is through thinking it through — working out what this situation needs and what it does not, until a path shows itself. Knowing where you are going before you go is what this looks like when it works, and the pull toward people returns on its own once that is settled. One clear line you can follow beats ten feelings you cannot sort.

cells.tense: You are already letting this go and calling it something else, pen down in a room you are still writing in.
cells.ask: Say to one person, in your own words, what you have already decided to let go of and why.
cells.core:
You are already clearing this. You have stopped putting in work, stopped explaining it the same way, started making room — and you would describe all of it as just being realistic, or busy, or over it. The ending is underway and you are the one doing it.

What is missing is owning it. You are the one deciding what stays and what goes, and you do not say so out loud, which leaves it feeling like something happening to you. Nothing grand has to be announced. One true sentence to one person about what you have already chosen to let go of, and the room belongs to you again.
